scene.note: Fares.java turns the clipboard's whole numbers into prices, trips, an average and ticket numbers, choosing the type each answer needs.

steps.note: The clipboard has the single fare in whole pence.
A return is two single fares, with a little taken off for buying both.
The return fare is a whole number of pence, worked out in the right order.
A long queue waits on the quay, and the boat takes a fixed number a trip.
Dividing two whole numbers counts the full boatloads and drops the rest.
What was dropped is not lost: another operator gives the people left on the quay.
Ossian logs the passengers today and the crossings today, both whole numbers.
Divided as whole numbers, the part after the point is gone before it is stored.
With one side turned into a decimal first, the average keeps every part.
A ticket number is the date code with five digits for the ticket of the day after it.
Moving the date code five places along makes a number far bigger than an int holds.
Worked out as a long from the start, the ticket number comes out whole and right.
